title: Division 152 — CGT small business concessions
summary: Four CGT concessions for small business — the 15-year exemption, the 50% reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over. All require the Subdivision 152-A basic conditions: a CGT event producing a gain, a CGT small business entity or $6M net asset value test, and the active asset test. The 15-year exemption has priority; the retirement exemption and roll-over apply (in either order) to the gain left after the 50% reduction. Key interaction provisions: the CGT concession stakeholder definition (s 152-110), the CGT cap amount for retirement contributions (s 152-325), the replacement asset period (s 104-190), recapture events J2/J5/J6 (ss 104-185, 104-197, 104-198), and the net capital gain method statement (s 102-5). Subsection coverage: operative ss 152-10, 152-12, 152-15, 152-20, 152-35, 152-40, 152-45, 152-105, 152-110, 152-115, 152-125, 152-205, 152-210, 152-305, 152-315, 152-325, 152-410, 152-415, 152-430, 104-185, 104-190, 104-197, 104-198, 102-5 mapped to nodes; ss 152-1, 152-5, 152-47, 152-48, 152-49, 152-50, 152-55, 152-60, 152-65, 152-70, 152-75, 152-78, 152-80, 152-100, 152-200, 152-215, 152-220, 152-300, 152-310, 152-320, 152-330, 152-400, 152-420 (machinery/definitional/transitional).

nodes.label: You carry on a business and a CGT event happens in relation to a CGT asset used in it (or shares/units in a company or trust that carries on the business)
nodes.body: Division 152 lets a small business reduce or disregard capital gains from CGT events involving business (active) assets. There are four concessions: the 15-year exemption (Subdiv 152-B), the 50% reduction (Subdiv 152-C), the retirement exemption (Subdiv 152-D) and the roll-over (Subdiv 152-E). All require the basic conditions in Subdivision 152-A to be satisfied first.

nodes.label: A CGT event happens in relation to a CGT asset of yours in an income year
nodes.body: A CGT event happens in relation to a CGT asset of yours in an income year (s 152-10(1)(a) — not applicable to event D1, see s 152-12). Check the special rule at s 152-10(4): events J2/J5/J6 are excluded from some concessions.

nodes.label: Would the event (apart from this Division) result in a capital gain?
nodes.body: The concessions apply only to gains. If the event produces a capital loss (or neither gain nor loss), the basic conditions are not satisfied and no small business concession is available for that event.

nodes.label: Are you a CGT small business entity, or do you satisfy the maximum net asset value test (≤ $6M)?
nodes.body: CGT small business entity (s 152-10(1)(c)(i)): you are a small business entity (aggregated turnover under $10M, s 328-110) and would still be one if the $10M threshold were $2M (s 152-10(1AA)). Alternatively, the maximum net asset value test (s 152-10(1)(c)(ii), s 152-15) is satisfied if the net value of your CGT assets plus those of entities connected with you and your affiliates does not exceed $6M just before the CGT event. Assets excluded from net value are set out in s 152-20(2)-(4). The partner carve-out (s 152-10(1)(c)(iii)) and the passive asset conditions (s 152-10(1)(c)(iv), ss 152-10(1A)-(1B)) are alternative paths.

nodes.body: A partner in a partnership that is a CGT small business entity can qualify for the concessions in relation to an interest in an asset of the partnership without separately satisfying the turnover or net asset tests (s 152-10(1)(c)(iii)).

nodes.label: Do the passively-held asset conditions apply (s 152-10(1A) or (1B))?
nodes.body: s 152-10(1A): (a) your affiliate, or an entity connected with you, is a CGT SBE; (b) you do not carry on a business in the year (other than in partnership); (c) if you carry on a business in partnership — the CGT asset is NOT an interest in an asset of the partnership; (d) the CGT SBE is the entity that carries on the business in relation to the asset. s 152-10(1B): (a) you are a partner in a partnership; (b) the partnership is a CGT SBE; (c) you carry on no business other than in partnership; (d) the asset is not an interest in a partnership asset; (e) the partnership business is the business carried on in relation to the asset. Either path satisfies the entity-size condition.

nodes.label: Does the asset satisfy the active asset test?
nodes.body: Owned for 15 years or less: the asset must have been an active asset of yours for a total of at least half the period from acquisition to the earlier of the CGT event and (if the business ceased in the previous 12 months, or longer if the Commissioner allows) the cessation (s 152-35(1)(a)). Owned for more than 15 years: at least 7½ years in that period (s 152-35(1)(b)). For involuntary disposals (compulsory acquisition, loss or destruction) the time periods continue under s 152-45. The meaning of active asset is in s 152-40.

nodes.label: Is the asset an active asset — used in a business carried on by you, your affiliate or a connected entity?
nodes.body: An asset is active if it is used, or held ready for use, in carrying on a business (alone or in partnership) by you, your affiliate or a connected entity; an intangible asset is active if it is inherently connected with such a business (for example goodwill). Shares in a company or interests in a trust are active assets where at least 80% of the entity's assets by market value are active assets or business-connected financial instruments or cash (s 152-40(3)). Excluded assets: financial instruments, assets whose main use is deriving rent, interest, royalties or foreign exchange gains (with limited exceptions), and interests in connected entities outside the 80% rule (s 152-40(4)).

nodes.body: Shares and trust interests attract additional basic conditions under s 152-10(2), including the extended active asset assumptions in s 152-10(2A)-(2B) and the CGT concession stakeholder test.

nodes.label: Do the additional basic conditions for shares/trust interests apply (s 152-10(2))?
nodes.body: s 152-10(2) additional conditions where the asset is a share in a company or interest in a trust (the object entity): (a) the asset satisfies the active asset test under the s 152-10(2A) extended assumptions; (b) if you do not satisfy the NAVA test — you carry on a business just before the CGT event; (c) the object entity would be a CGT SBE or satisfy the NAVA test on the s 152-10(2C) assumptions (only its own + affiliates' + controlled entities' assets/turnover, 20% control threshold, no s 328-125(6) determination); (d) just before the event you are a CGT concession stakeholder in the object entity, or CGT concession stakeholders together hold at least 90% of the object entity's market value. Any failure → concessions unavailable.

nodes.label: Basic conditions satisfied — apply the concessions in order: 15-year exemption first, then 50% reduction, then retirement exemption and/or roll-over
nodes.body: s 152-430: the 15-year exemption has priority — a gain it covers is entirely disregarded and no other concession applies. Otherwise the 50% reduction applies automatically to the gain remaining after step 3 of the method statement (the general discount). The retirement exemption and the roll-over can then apply to the reduced gain, in either order, or both (s 152-210).

statute.title: You may also get the small business retirement exemption and small business roll-over relief

nodes.label: 15-year exemption: have you continuously owned the asset for 15+ years and are you retiring or permanently incapacitated?
nodes.body: Individual (s 152-105): basic conditions satisfied; continuous ownership for the 15 years ending just before the event; if the asset is shares/units, the company or trust must have had a significant individual for a total of at least 15 years during your ownership; and you are 55 or over with the event connected with your retirement, or you are permanently incapacitated. Company or trust (s 152-110): same ownership and significant-individual rules, and a significant individual just before the event is 55+/retiring or permanently incapacitated. Time periods continue for involuntary disposals and certain roll-overs (s 152-115).

nodes.label: 15-year exemption: the entire capital gain is disregarded
nodes.body: The gain is wholly disregarded (s 152-105 for individuals; s 152-110 for companies and trusts, which also makes related ordinary/statutory income non-assessable non-exempt). The company or trust can then make exempt payments to its CGT concession stakeholders within the limits in s 152-125. Because this concession has priority, no other concession applies to the gain.

nodes.label: 50% reduction: the gain remaining after the general discount is reduced by a further 50%
nodes.body: s 152-205 reduces by 50% the amount remaining after step 3 of the method statement in s 102-5(1) (the general 50% discount for individuals and trusts, or indexation where chosen). For an individual the combined effect eliminates up to 75% of the original gain before any further concession. A company (no discount) gets only the 50% reduction. This reduction is automatic once the basic conditions are satisfied.

nodes.label: Retirement exemption: do you choose to disregard all or part of the remaining gain? (Subdiv 152-D)
nodes.body: Individual (s 152-305(1)): choose to disregard all or part of the gain if the basic conditions are satisfied; if you are under 55 just before the choice, you must contribute an amount equal to the asset's CGT exempt amount to a complying superannuation fund or RSA (at the choice time, or when you receive the proceeds; instalments are dealt with in s 152-305(1A)). Company or trust (s 152-305(2)): the significant individual test must be satisfied and the payment conditions in s 152-325 met. Entities in s 328-125(8) cannot choose.

nodes.label: Is the choice within the CGT retirement exemption limit ($500,000 lifetime per individual)?
nodes.body: s 152-315: the choice must be made so that the individual's CGT retirement exemption limit is not exceeded ($500,000 lifetime — see the example in s 152-315). The CGT exempt amount must be specified in writing; a company or trust choosing must specify the percentage of each asset's CGT exempt amount attributable to each CGT concession stakeholder. Amounts not chosen remain taxable.

nodes.label: Retirement exemption: the gain is disregarded up to the CGT exempt amount chosen
nodes.body: All or part of the gain is disregarded up to the CGT exempt amount (s 152-305, s 152-315). For an individual under 55 the disregarded amount must be contributed to super. The remaining gain can then go to the roll-over if chosen.

nodes.label: Roll-over: do you choose it for the remaining gain? (Subdiv 152-E)
nodes.body: You can choose the roll-over under s 152-410 if the basic conditions are satisfied — even before acquiring a replacement asset. If by the end of the replacement asset period you have not acquired a replacement asset (or incurred fourth element expenditure), CGT event J5 recaptures the disregarded gain (s 104-197); if the amount spent is less than the disregarded gain, CGT event J6 recaptures the difference (s 104-198).

nodes.label: Do you acquire a replacement asset (or incur fourth element expenditure) by the end of the replacement asset period?
nodes.body: The replacement asset period (s 104-190) starts one year before the last CGT event in the income year for which you obtain the roll-over and ends at the later of 2 years after that event and, for a disposal, 6 months after the latest time a possible financial benefit becomes due under a look-through earnout right. The Commissioner may extend the period. It is modified if capital proceeds are later increased under ss 116-45 or 116-60.

nodes.label: Is the replacement asset your active asset at the end of the replacement asset period (and, for shares/units, is the stakeholder test met)?
nodes.body: The replacement asset must be an active asset (s 104-197(2)). For shares or trust interests, you (or an entity connected with you) must be a CGT concession stakeholder in the company or trust, or CGT concession stakeholders must have a small business participation percentage in you of at least 90%. A later change in relation to the replacement asset triggers CGT event J2 (s 104-185).

nodes.label: Roll-over: the gain is disregarded and the replacement asset's cost base is reduced by the disregarded amount
nodes.body: s 152-415: you can disregard all or part of the remaining gain. The first element of the replacement asset's cost base is reduced by the disregarded amount, so the gain is deferred into the replacement asset rather than forgiven. You can choose to disregard only part of the gain and keep the rest taxable.

nodes.label: No qualifying replacement by period end — CGT event J5 or J6 recaptures the disregarded gain
nodes.body: If no replacement asset is acquired (or fourth element expenditure incurred) by the end of the replacement asset period, CGT event J5 happens at that time and you make a capital gain equal to the amount disregarded under the roll-over (s 104-197). If a replacement is acquired but the total cost is less than the disregarded gain, CGT event J6 recaptures the difference (s 104-198). The Commissioner may extend the period.

nodes.label: Concessions applied — the reduced gain feeds into the net capital gain calculation
nodes.body: Up to 100% of the gain can be eliminated (15-year exemption) or reduced in combination (50% reduction plus retirement exemption and/or roll-over, in the chosen order). The remaining gain is included in your net capital gain under s 102-5.

nodes.label: Is the CGT event J2, J5 or J6? (s 152-10(4))
nodes.body: s 152-10(4): Subdivisions 152-B (15-year exemption) and 152-C (50% reduction) do NOT apply to CGT events J2, J5 and J6; Subdivision 152-E (roll-over) does not apply to J5 and J6. These events concern previous applications of the 152-E roll-over. If the event is J2/J5/J6, the small business concessions are unavailable for this gain (subject to the Subdiv 152-B retirement exemption note at s 152-305(4) for J5/J6).

nodes.label: Does s 152-10(2C) apply — CGT event involving a partnership right/interest? (s 152-10(2C))
nodes.body: s 152-10(2C): if the CGT event involves the creation, transfer, variation or cessation of a right or interest entitling an entity to (a) an amount of the income or capital of a partnership, or (b) an amount calculated by reference to a partner's entitlement to income/capital of a partnership, it is an additional basic condition that the right or interest is a membership interest of the entity in the partnership immediately after the event (or, for cessation, immediately before). If it is not a membership interest, the concessions do not apply.
